questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, you should:
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an object, try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as possible before impact. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel just before you hit it.

questions.question: As a rider, you should prepare a passenger to ride by instructing them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large distance between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large distance between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Before riding, tell your passenger to get on only after the engine starts. They should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you. They should hold the passenger handholds or hold your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: When following a car, the best lane position to ride in is usually:
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when following a car. This position makes you visible in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors, so this helps them see you.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Signs that show traffic rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: How can you prevent another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Swerve back and forth in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must have all of the following, except:

options.text: Be so tight that sunglasses or eyeglasses cannot be worn.
Allow clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be so tight that sunglasses or eyeglasses cannot be worn.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist breaking, allow clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Which of the following is a poor reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is too close to the car ahead.
Someone is sitting in the driver's seat of a parked car.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing someone in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn before passing a vehicle or pedestrian who might move into your lane. Use it if a nearby driver seems ready to merge into your path, if someone is sitting in a parked car, or if you see a pedestrian or bicyclist in the street. Do not use it just to get attention.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Use arms to hold their body up.
Keep their knees away from the gas tank.
Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent on the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Help you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.
Put you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your lane position should keep other drivers from sharing your lane and should give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Spread out so the group is easier to see.
Stay close together so the group is easier to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together so the group is easier to see.
questions.explanation: Stay close together as a group while leaving enough space around each rider to move safely. Staying close makes the group more visible and prevents riders from getting separated. Do not ride in pairs because this does not allow enough room to maneuver.

questions.question: When packing a load on a motorcycle, where should you place the heavier items?

options.text: In front of you with lighter items.

questions.explanation: Place heavier items toward the front of the load. Keep the load over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should stay just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the inexperienced rider lead the group.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
Pull over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is tailgating you. They may not see hazards ahead that require traffic to slow down.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week. Regular inspections help keep your motorcycle safe to ride.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the drinker usually drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker usually drinks
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and the drinker's body weight. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.
